subject: Request: TTFT smoothing heuristic & sustained tokens carveout for pilot
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@acme-corp.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: sre+acme@acme-corp.com, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot request: TTFT smoothing & sustained token targets

Hi Michael / team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked promising. Our SRE and product teams reviewed the hosted SLA and we have one ask for the pilot: Acme generates a high number of short-lived streaming sessions (chat-like UX with lots of single-turn queries). For the pilot we need an explicit carveout so that time-to-first-token (TTFT) is measured with a 200ms smoothing window for bursty traffic, and a separate sustained token/sec expectation (samples/sec) for sessions longer than 4s.

Specifically wed like: 
- TTFT: 95th percentile <= 350ms with ability to tolerate bursts where instantaneous TTFT may spike to ~800ms for up to 60s, provided smoothing window averages back to <=350ms.
- Sustained tokens/s: >= 18 tokens/s for sustained responses (after prefix warm-start).

Can Redwood propose language we can include in the SOW and confirm whether this can be supported on Hosted with a pilot SLA? Im attaching a short note from our SRE that explains our traffic shape.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp

Attachment: 2026-09-12_acme_ttft_request.txt (text, 3KB)
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request: TTFT smoothing & sustained token targets

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear ask and the SRE note. We can support a pilot with explicit measurement boundaries; below is a draft proposal wed be comfortable committing to for a 3-month pilot on Hosted (we can move to Dedicated later if needed):

Proposal (pilot SLA language draft)
- TTFT measurement: 95th percentile TTFT measured on the per-request first-byte timestamp over a sliding 60s window. A smoothing window of 200ms will be used to discount micro-variance from downstream network queuing. Committed target: 95p <= 350ms over the sliding window.
- Burst carveout: For short burst events, transient spikes to 800ms are permitted for up to 60s per 30m interval provided the 60s sliding window average returns to <=350ms.
- Sustained throughput: For responses (after KV/prefix warm-start), sustained token emission rate will target >=18 tokens/sec for sustained responses (>4s). Measured across the same sliding window with a minimum sample count of N=30 responses.
- Fallback & routing: During capacity constraints, traffic will be routed to a compatible lower-cost variant with documented degradation; Redwood will provide real-time routing logs and a fallback plan.

Next steps: Aditya, can you confirm feasibility on our runtime (prefers quantized LLMs + prefix caching) and whether we need a reserved burst pool to satisfy the 18 tokens/s target? Lauren, Ill draft wording for the SOW. Elaine, happy to sync this afternoon if helpful.

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: smoothing_proposal.pdf referenced — draft language + measurement diagrams)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 14:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request: TTFT smoothing & sustained token targets

Michael — quick technical note from infra: we can implement the 200ms smoothing on TTFT at the edge collector (we already capture first-byte times and per-token emission timestamps). A few implementation details to call out:

- Warm path: If a request can hit a cached KV prefix (same user context), TTFT drops substantially; for Acmes UX profile we should include a prefix-warm metric and exclude warm-starts from the strictest burst counting.
- Burst pool: To guarantee >=18 tokens/s for sustained responses, I recommend a small reserved GPU burst pool during the pilot (idle capacity pinned to the account). Without a reserved pool the hosted allocator may schedule on shared capacity and sustained tokens/s could vary.
- Measurement tooling: Well expose per-request traces and a 60s sliding window dashboard. The sustained token/sec will be computed across response emission timestamps, excluding responses shorter than 400ms to avoid noise.

Risk: The main variance source is cold model load (KV cache miss + cold scheduler). With the reserved burst pool and prefix warm-start exclusions we can be confident in meeting the proposed targets for the pilot.

Aditya
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request: TTFT smoothing & sustained token targets

Short commercial note: if Acme wants a reserved burst pool for the 3-month pilot wed include a modest monthly commitment to cover the reserved capacity (pricing to be added to the SOW). We can offer an optional SLA credit if measured sliding-window TTFT exceeds the target by >25% for more than 2 consecutive measurement windows.

Michael — Ill take the draft language and add a short carveout section for prefix-warm-starts and the SLA credit threshold. Aditya — please add a simple dashboard screenshot so Acme can validate measurement. Rachel, can you prepare the pricing delta?

Lauren Bishop
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Elaine Park <elaine@acme-corp.com>

Cc: sre+acme@acme-corp.com, procurement@acme-corp.com

Subject: Re: Pilot request: TTFT smoothing & sustained token targets

Michael / team — this looks good and thanks for the detailed tradeoffs. Acme is willing to accept a 3-month pilot with a small reserved burst pool and the smoothing language you proposed. Two quick asks before SOW:

1) Please explicitly exclude prefix-warm starts from burst-window compliance checks (we need that excluded for our UX measurement).
2) Can Redwood provide a shared dashboard link and a weekly sample CSV export for the pilot?

If you can confirm those items and share the updated SOW + pricing, procurement will circulate for signature. Attaching procurement contact details.

Elaine
(Procurement cc: procurement@acme-corp.com)
